record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: For every sufficiently wide branching program of width w and length ℓ, is there an equivalent branching program of width w − 1 and length poly(ℓ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Show that for any branching program B of sufficiently large width w and length ℓ, there exists a branching program B ′ of width w − 1 and length poly (ℓ) computing the same function.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A (deterministic) branching program of width $w$ and length $\ell$ over Boolean input variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$ is a sequence of $\ell$ instructions $I_1,\dots,I_\ell$ acting on a state space $[w]=\{1,\dots,w\}$. Each instruction $I_t$ specifies an input index $i_t\in[n]$ and two functions $f_t^0,f_t^1:[w]\to[w]$; on input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the program starts in state $1$ and updates the current state $s$ to $f_t^{x_{i_t}}(s)$ at step $t$. The program computes a Boolean function of $x$ determined by whether the final state lies in a designated accepting subset of $[w]$. Two branching programs are equivalent if they compute the same function.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $w_0$ such that for every $w\ge w_0$ and every branching program $B$ of width $w$ and length $\ell$, there is an equivalent branching program $B'$ of width $w-1$ and length $\mathrm{poly}(\ell)$.
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found establishing the claimed width-by-one reduction with polynomial length blow-up for general branching programs. Classical results (Barrington's theorem) show width 5 suffices to capture NC^1, and width-4 polynomial-size branching programs also capture NC^1, but a generic step-down from width w to width w-1 at polynomial cost is not known and is listed as an open problem in current literature on reusing space.

status_evidence.title: Bounded-Width Polynomial-Size Branching Programs Recognize Exactly Those Languages in NC1
status_evidence.snippet: Width-5 polynomial-size branching programs recognize exactly nonuniform NC^1.
status_evidence.claim: Barrington's theorem gives width-5 simulation of NC^1, but does not establish a general w to w-1 reduction with polynomial length.
